clue.text: One does the Lord's work!

parts.note: the surface suggests a priest or missionary, but Jesus worked at a trade before his ministry, as the son of Joseph the woodworker

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising someone devoted to religious service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lord's work' sounds like church duty; read literally it is the trade Jesus is said to have practised in Nazareth.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus is traditionally described as a woodworker by trade, so his earthly work was joinery.

clue.text: Conspirator responsible for rent about to occupy house in Spain

indicators.note: the letter for about occupies, sits inside, the house

parts.note: casa is Spanish for house
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A plotter who handles a landlord's rent around a Spanish house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for housing; it is the tear in Caesar's mantle, from Julius Caesar: 'See what a rent the envious Casca made'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the assassins of Julius Caesar, who in Shakespeare struck the first blow and tore the cloak.

clue.text: Sharp rebuke quietly ignored by MP over the moon with new plant

indicators.note: ignored means the musical abbreviation for quietly is left out

parts.note: a rap is a sharp telling-off
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
taken as written
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A politician, ecstatic about a new plant, ignores a quiet scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the moon' tempts as delight; 'over' is only placement in a down clue, and the moon is Jupiter's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellflower whose roots were once eaten as a vegetable, a type of plant.

clue.text: Recast in role under consideration quite recently

indicators.note: in a down clue the reworked letters sit under, after, the first piece

parts.note: ear means attention or consideration, as in giving someone a hearing

indicators.note: recast means reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor recast in a part that producers are still weighing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recast' rearranges IN ROLE into LIERON, which goes under EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at a time not long past, before now in the same day or period.

clue.text: Rewritten by Lear — still amusing as an example!

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are written out again in another order

explanation.surface: A line of Edward Lear's verse, rewritten, is still funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: 'amusing' has three syllables. Edward Lear was a writer of nonsense verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word amusing has three syllables, so it is one example of a word of that kind.

clue.text: Ridicule piece Joplin would compose

definitions.meaning: Scott Joplin composed ragtime pieces such as The Entertainer

explanation.surface: Mocking the kind of music Scott Joplin wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is a sense of the verb, and a ragtime tune is the noun sense.

clue.text: Along with first couple from Essex in Peak District

parts.note: along with means and

indicators.note: the first couple of letters, the opening pair, are taken from the word Essex

explanation.surface: Directions for a trip combining Essex with the hills of Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak District' looks like the English national park; read literally it is a region of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American mountain range is a whole region full of high summits, a literal district of peaks.

clue.text: Own daughter married in small island

indicators.note: the two abbreviations are placed in the island word

parts.note: an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: A man owns up that his daughter married on a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Own' is a verb here: to own up, confess.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fault is to confess or acknowledge it; the verb sense, not possession.

clue.text: What might be ideal as accommodation for male pairing causes problem

indicators.note: the reworked letters provide accommodation for the doubled letter
what might be ideal means letters that could be rearranged to spell it
pairing means the letter for male is used twice

explanation.surface: Finding ideal housing for a male couple poses a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What might be ideal' rearranges IDEAL into DILEA, which takes in MM.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice between two awkward options is a tricky problem.

clue.text: Society —— group into wine — gets tight

indicators.note: the group goes into the wine

parts.note: tent is a dark red Spanish wine
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A society group drinking wine becomes tight, meaning drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like drunk; it means strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict or severe rules are tight ones, with no slack.

clue.text: Drink with arsenic knocked back by very fit warriors

indicators.note: knocked back means the drink and the arsenic, written together, are read backwards

parts.note: rum is a drink
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
A1 means first-rate, in fine shape; the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A poisoned drink is swallowed by some very fit fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses RUM and AS together to give SAMUR. A1 stands for excellent, with the 1 used as an I.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the hereditary military class of feudal Japan were fighting men.

clue.text: Gaining access to King George walk at leisurely pace — it's better!

indicators.note: the stroll gains access to, getting inside, the royal abbreviation

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
to amble is to walk slowly

explanation.surface: Someone strolling in to see the king, apparently an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good; here it means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places bets on outcomes is a punter, so a person who bets can be called a better.

clue.text: Defence starts off arguing legal issues behind injunction

indicators.note: the starts, the initial letters, are taken off each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A lawyer's defence begins by challenging the legal basis of a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of having been elsewhere at the time of a crime is a plea in defence.

clue.text: Sailor may snatch rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are strangely rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman might grab some rum, the traditional naval spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the sailor's drink, but here it is the adjective meaning odd, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a leisure boat is a sailor.

clue.text: Dictator raised as extrovert man leaves meal that's tasty

parts.note: Julius Caesar was dictator of Rome

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word as is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a lively, outgoing young man, a bit of a lad

explanation.surface: A dictator raised as an outgoing man leaves to have a tasty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb for departing; it is the salad's lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of lettuce leaves with croutons, Parmesan and dressing; leaves make it a meal.

clue.text: Popular name for pub

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A well-liked name chosen for a public house.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern or public house offering drink and lodging; a simple synonym.

clue.text: Bring about flexibility in eating this with husband away

indicators.note: flexibility in the letters means they bend into a new order
away means the letter for husband is taken out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Bringing about some leeway in eating this without the husband around.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of EATING THIS less H are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to bring about or provoke an action; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fish on huge wave use device for smooth travel

indicators.note: in an across clue, fish on huge wave puts the fish after the wave

parts.note: a roller is a big breaking wave
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish riding a big wave, as if surfing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot or frame with wheels lets the wearer glide along pavements.

clue.text: Spectator may observe from here teams holding course

indicators.note: the teams word holds the course inside it

parts.note: sides are teams
a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: A spectator watching teams on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The area just outside the pitch boundaries is where onlookers and substitutes watch from.

clue.text: Help with launch to get directors out of jail

definitions.meaning: a flexible board that helps a diver or gymnast launch into the air
to spring is to free from prison, and the board is a company's directors

explanation.surface: A plan to help a business launch by freeing its jailed directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving or vaulting board, and figuratively anything that gives a start, helps a launch.

clue.text: Hawk-headed god, very old, with wrecked appearance

parts.note: Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a hawk's head
aged means old

explanation.surface: An ancient Egyptian deity looking battered with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid waste and devastated, so looking wrecked.

clue.text: Witty words being second and third from author

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: the third letter is taken from the word author

explanation.surface: A writer's clever remarks come in quick succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second and third' looks like a pair of positions in author; only 'third' is, and 'second' is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty saying or quip, as in bon mot; a crossword-favoured French borrowing.

clue.text: Spring month lovely to see in smart residential district

parts.note: May is a spring month
fair means good-looking

explanation.surface: A spring month is lovely in a fashionable part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYFAIR is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: An expensive area of London's West End, a smart place to live.

clue.text: Aboard steamer carrying writer coming to northern city

indicators.note: the steamship phrase carries the writer within it

parts.note: aboard is in
SS stands for steamship
Jules Verne, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist travels by steamship to a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer sits between the two halves of 'aboard steamer'; 'northern' is part of the definition, not an N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland capital of Scotland, a city in the far north of Britain.

clue.text: Pirate runs past

parts.note: R for runs in cricket
over means finished, past

explanation.surface: A pirate dashes by.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is an old word for a sea robber or freebooter.

clue.text: Productive hen always held in both hands

indicators.note: the word for always is held within the two hands

parts.note: L and R, left and right
aye is an old word for always, ever

explanation.surface: A good egg-producing hen held carefully in both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen that lays eggs well is a good egg-producer.

clue.text: Quick to decode the unknown

parts.note: to read is to decode or interpret
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone quick at cracking codes, even with an unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means prompt, quick to respond, as in a ready wit.

clue.text: Plantagenet excited Vienna with grand entrance

indicators.note: the letter for grand makes an entrance into the rearranged city
excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A medieval royal arrives in Vienna in great style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges VIENNA to ANEVIN, and G goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenet kings descended from the Counts of Anjou, so a member of that house is from Anjou.

clue.text: Raul Sanguineti beaten all ends up for nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards
the ends, last letters, of all three words are taken

explanation.surface: An Argentine footballer is beaten on the scoreboard, his side scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Raul Sanguineti was an Argentine footballer of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is zero, the usual word for nothing in a football score.

clue.text: Having role in Shakespeare, staying home with a script yet to be read

indicators.note: having means containing, so the role holds the next piece

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespeare title role
in means at home

explanation.surface: An actor playing a Shakespeare role stays home learning an unread script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'script yet to be read' sounds like an actor's homework; it means a writing system no one has deciphered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minoan writing system of ancient Crete has never been deciphered, so it is a script still unread.

clue.text: Ancestor found for wifeless worker at seam

indicators.note: wifeless means the abbreviation W for wife is removed

parts.note: a welder joins metal along a seam

explanation.surface: A forebear identified as a bachelor miner working a coal seam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seam' suggests a coal miner, but it is a welded joint.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person, a forebear of an earlier generation, as in the elders of a tribe.

clue.text: Persuaded to take wrong course having ordered salted fish

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone tempted into a bad choice by ordering salted fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like choosing from a menu; it rearranges SALTED into LEDAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Misled or tempted away from the right path; the phrase means exactly that.
